text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-prod-gpu' p99 latency spike > 5x baseline, streaming stalls detected, SLOs breached for routes: /v1/chat, /v1/stream. Queue depth rising. Paging oncall. https://internal.telemetry/redwood/alerts/7201112222

maya (oncall): seeing it, ack. pulling histograms now. p95 -> 420ms (x2), p99 -> 2.6s (x6). streaming stall rate ~8% recent 5m.

maya (oncall): initial hypothesis = dedicated pool saturation + autoscaler warmup lag. lots of warmup tasks queued.

jordan: on my way. quick question — any customer-facing errors? will check support dashboard.

priya: support dashboard shows increased errors for two large customers (acme and atlas) on streaming sessions: session resets and partial responses. CS already flagged both.

kevin (sre): looking at pool telemetry — GPU utilization 98%, handshake/warmup success rate dropped, heartbeat RTTs jittered. autoscaler attempted scale +2 but new nodes not joining fast enough.

maya (oncall): ops-bot, can we temporarily route high-priority customers to fallback model/region? priority routing config?

ops-bot: Routing playbooks available: use command `redwood route set-priority --pool eu-west-1-prod-gpu --customers acme,atlas --fallback eu-west-1-fallback-cpu`. Requires approver.

jordan: I'll handle manual fallback for the two customers to reduce load on GPU pool. Priya please coordinate CS message.

priya: will draft message now. ETA 3m.

kevin (sre): quick mitigation suggestions: 1) open temporary hotshot pool (reserve 3 gpus) 2) relax batching for streaming routes (reduce max_batch_size) 3) force immediate scaleup (bypass cooldown) 4) enable model-variant fallback (quantized) for non-streaming requests.

maya (oncall): do we have hotshot capacity available?

kevin (sre): yes, spare capacity in eu-west-1-standby; can hotshot 3 GPUs in ~90s. Command: ```infractl pool hotshot create --region eu-west-1 --count 3 --tags incident-7201112222```

maya (oncall): executing now.```

[system] maya (oncall) executed: infractl pool hotshot create --region eu-west-1 --count 3 --tags incident-7201112222 (started)

jordan: I'm running the route change to fallback model for acme/atlas. Command: ```redwood route set-priority --pool eu-west-1-prod-gpu --customers acme,atlas --fallback eu-west-1-fallback-cpu```

[jordan] executed route change — verified traffic shifting ~60% off GPU pool for those customers.

maya (oncall): we still see p99 ~2.1s but streaming stall rate dropped to 3.5%. queue depth decreased by ~40%. Good initial signal.

priya: CS message posted to acme/atlas: short heads-up + mitigation + ETA. (emoji :thumbsup:)

kevin (sre): hotshot pool joining now, nodes starting containers, warmup logs show model KV-cache initialization in progress. warmup tasks being drained from queue.

maya (oncall): important note: autoscaler logs show JOIN_TIMEOUT for 2 nodes — investigating handshake timeouts between control-plane and private pools. Could be heartbeat drift after config push.

kevin (sre): confirming: control-plane heartbeat TTL was 10s, some nodes responded at ~18-22s during surge. Proposal: temporarily increase TTL tolerance to 30s and retry scale join attempts more aggressively. This avoids aborting warmup prematurely.

jordan: can we flip that config safely? risk?

kevin (sre): low-risk for short window. I'll make the change and monitor. Command: ```infractl config set autoscaler.heartbeat_ttl 30 --scope eu-west-1 --temporary 30m```

kevin (sre): applied. Also bumped scale retry to 3 attempts.

maya (oncall): hotshot nodes warmed. Observed KV cache hit rate increasing, streaming stall rate now 1.1%, p99 down to 860ms, p95 380ms.

sarah (product): any customer impact left? do we need to open a livepage for execs?

priya: acme reported degraded experience but not critical. atlas had transient resets but now stable. CS will escalate if they see regressions. recommend no exec livepage yet, but continue monitoring 30m.

jordan: next steps for post-incident: 1) investigate handshake/heartbeat drift root cause 2) add pre-warm for standby hotshot nodes when signals show queue depth > threshold 3) tune autoscaler to prefer gradual extra capacity rather than aborting warmup 4) improve routing priority automation to divert only necessary sessions instead of whole-customer fallback.

maya (oncall): agree. Also capture reproducer for streaming stall — include long-running low-throughput sessions which hold KV caches and cause batch starvation. Need to consider per-session priority lanes.

kevin (sre): filing incident ticket and assigning owners. ETA: initial RCA doc in 24h, full postmortem in 72h. Ticket: INC-7201112222 (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-7201112222)

priya: CS follow-up templates ready. I'll coordinate customer debriefs after RCA.

maya (oncall): handing back to oncall rotation: jordan will own active mitigation follow-ups for the next 30m, then rotate. tagging @jordan.

jordan: on it. thanks team. :metal:

incident-bot: [RESOLUTION] Alert cleared — p99 back within SLO. Monitoring until 7201112560.
